summary: צִוָּה is to lay a charge on someone: one who has the right to be obeyed tells another what he is to do or not to do, and the other is then bound to do it. Its first use is Yahweh God's charge to the man in the garden (Gen 2:16), and most of its uses are Yahweh's: what he commanded Moses, the covenant he commanded Israel, the creation that stood when he commanded (Psa 33:9), the ravens, the clouds and the blessing that go where he orders. A father charges his sons, a king his servants, a dying man his house; to charge a man over a people is to appoint him its ruler (1Sa 13:14). מִצְוָה is the thing commanded: a king's or a father's order, and above all the commandments of Yahweh, which Israel is to keep and do, set beside his statutes, judgments, testimonies and law. צַו is a single precept (Isa 28:10), and צִיּוּן is a marker of stones set up by a road or a grave, as Arabic ṣuwwa is; Arabic waṣṣā “enjoin, charge”, with the first two consonants in the other order, has the verb's sense.

words.gloss: command, charge; appoint; order into being
words.summary: Close to five hundred times, only in the piel and its passive, the pual. The one charged is its object (“Yahweh commanded Moses”), or stands after עַל, אֶל or לְ; the thing charged follows as speech (“saying”), as an infinitive, or as a second object (“the covenant which he commanded you”). Four tokens counted with the verb are the noun צַו of Isa 28:10, 13, spelled like the imperative.

stems.gloss: command, charge; give a last charge; charge with an office, appoint; order (a thing) to come or to be

senses.gloss: command, charge (a person to do something)
senses.definition: To tell someone, with authority, what he is to do or not to do, so that he is bound to do it: God to man, a father to his sons, a master to his servants, a king to his people. The answer to it is doing “according to all that he commanded”, or not keeping it.

evidence.note: The first use: “Yahweh God וַיְצַו the man, saying, Of every tree of the garden you may freely eat”, and of one tree, “you shall not eat” (Gen 2:17). A command is spoken to a person, and both permits and forbids.
“Have you eaten of the tree which צִוִּיתִיךָ not to eat of?”: the command can be a prohibition, and eating is the breach of it.
“Noah did according to all that God צִוָּה him; so he did”: what is commanded is there to be done.
A father's charge: “Jonadab son of Rechab our father צִוָּה us, saying, You shall drink no wine, you nor your sons, for ever”; his sons kept it (Jer 35:14).
Abraham “will command his sons and his house after him, and they will keep the way of Yahweh”.
A master to his servants: Joseph commanded, and they filled the sacks with grain.
Absalom to his young men: “Strike Amnon … have not I commanded you?” The one who commands bears the deed.
Mordecai “did according to all that Esther had commanded him”.
“You shall speak all that אֲצַוֶּךָּ”: the prophet says what he is charged to say. So Jer 1:7; 26:2.
Of the prophet like Moses: “I will put my words in his mouth, and he shall speak to them all that אֲצַוֶּנּוּ.”
“You shall not add to the word which I מְצַוֶּה you, nor take from it”: what is commanded is fixed, neither more nor less. So Deu 13:1.
“His covenant which he צִוָּה you to do, the ten words”: the covenant is commanded. So Jos 7:11; Jdg 2:20; Psa 111:9.
“As Yahweh commanded Moses”: the refrain of the making of the dwelling (Exo 39 and 40).
“This word I commanded them, saying, Listen to my voice, and I will be your God.”
Nadab and Abihu offered strange fire “which he had not commanded them”.
The burning of sons and daughters in the valley of the son of Hinnom, “which I did not command, nor did it come into my heart”. So Jer 19:5; 32:35.
“Remember the law of Moses my servant, which I commanded him in Horeb for all Israel.”
Psa 91:11 quoted (ἐντελεῖται). Also Luk 4:10.
Deu 18:18 answered: “the Father who sent me gave me a commandment, what I should say and what I should speak.”

senses.gloss: charge with a message or errand
senses.definition: To send someone with a charge to another person: the one charged is told what to say or do, and the one he is sent to stands after אֶל or עַל.

evidence.note: Jacob sent messengers to Esau “and commanded them, saying, Thus you shall say to my lord Esau”.
Yahweh “וַיְצַוֵּם to the sons of Israel and to Pharaoh king of Egypt, to bring the sons of Israel out”: a charge carried to others.
Esther called Hathach “and charged him to (עַל) Mordecai, to know what this was”. So Est 4:10.
“Charge them to their masters, saying, Thus says Yahweh of hosts.”
Ezra charged men to Iddo, “and I put words in their mouth to speak”.
Joseph's brothers “וַיְצַוּוּ to Joseph, saying, Your father commanded before his death”: both the errand and the last charge.

senses.gloss: give a last charge; set one's house in order
senses.definition: Of a man about to die: to charge his sons or his house with what is to be done after him.

evidence.note: Jacob “וַיְצַו them and said, I am being gathered to my people; bury me with my fathers”; when he “finished commanding his sons” he died (Gen 49:33), and they did “as he had commanded them” (Gen 50:12).
To Hezekiah: “צַו לְבֵיתֶךָ, for you are dying and shall not live.” So Isa 38:1.
Ahithophel “went to his house, to his city, and gave charge to his house (וַיְצַו אֶל־בֵּיתוֹ), and hanged himself”.
“The days of David drew near to die, and he charged Solomon his son.”

senses.definition: To put a man in an office by charging him: with a second object (נָגִיד, “ruler”) or with עַל “over”. The appointing is itself a command, and the man holds his place under it.

evidence.note: “Yahweh has sought for himself a man after his heart, וַיְצַוֵּהוּ יַהְוֶה לְנָגִיד over his people, because you have not kept what Yahweh commanded you”: the verb twice, appointing David and charging Saul.
Of Joshua: “set him before Eleazar the priest and before all the congregation, וְצִוִּיתָה him before their eyes”; Moses laid his hands on him “and charged him” (Num 27:23).
“וָאֲצַוֶּה Hanani my brother and Hananiah … over (עַל) Jerusalem.”
“From the day that I commanded judges over my people Israel.”
David: Yahweh “chose me … to appoint me ruler over the people of Yahweh”. So 1Sa 25:30.
David of Solomon: “him I have appointed to be ruler over Israel and over Judah.”
“From the day that he appointed me to be their governor in the land of Judah.”
Yahweh “charged Joshua son of Nun and said, Be strong and of good courage, for you shall bring the sons of Israel into the land”. So Deu 3:28; 31:14.
The participle as a title: “a witness to peoples I have given him, a ruler and מְצַוֵּה of peoples.”

senses.gloss: order (a thing) to be, to come or to act
senses.definition: Of Yahweh: to give the word by which a thing comes to be or is sent on its work. The heavens and their host, the morning, the clouds, the ravens, the serpent and the sword, and blessing, mercy and deliverance all come at his command; so does judgment on a people.

evidence.note: “He spoke, and it was; he צִוָּה, and it stood”: commanding set beside speaking, and the thing commanded comes to be. Verse 6: “by the word of Yahweh the heavens were made”.
Of the heavens, sun, moon and stars: “he commanded, and they were created.”
“My hands stretched out the heavens, and all their host צִוֵּיתִי.”
“Have you in your days commanded the morning?”
“Who is he that speaks and it comes to be, when the Lord has not commanded?”
“The ravens צִוִּיתִי to feed you there”: no word is spoken to Elijah's hearing, yet the ravens come. So the widow of 1Ki 17:9.
“The clouds I will command not to rain on it.” So Psa 78:23.
“From there I will command the serpent, and it shall bite them”; verse 4, “the sword, and it shall kill them”.
“וְצִוִּיתִי my blessing for you in the sixth year, and it shall make the produce for the three years.” So Deu 28:8.
“There Yahweh commanded the blessing: life for evermore.”
“By day Yahweh will command his mercy.” So Psa 44:5, “command the deliverances of Jacob”.
“His angels he will command for you, to keep you in all your ways.”
In judgment: “Yahweh has commanded concerning Jacob that those around him be his adversaries.” So Isa 23:11; Nam 1:14; Amo 9:9.
“Yahweh had commanded to break the good counsel of Ahithophel”: what he orders comes about through men who do not know it.

senses.definition: The passive of the piel: to be under a charge, said by the one charged of what he does or says (“as I was commanded”).

evidence.note: “I prophesied כַּאֲשֶׁר צֻוֵּיתִי”: answering “prophesy over these bones” (verse 4). So Ezk 12:7; 24:18.
“Moses numbered them at the mouth of Yahweh, as he was commanded.”
“You shall keep the charge of Yahweh, that you die not, for so I am commanded.” So Lev 10:13.
Pharaoh to Joseph: “you are commanded: do this.”
Moses spoke to the sons of Israel “what he was commanded”.

evidence.locator: Gen.2.16, וַיְצַו → ἐνετείλατο; Deu.18.18, אֲצַוֶּנּוּ → ἐντείλωμαι; Psa.33.9, צִוָּה → ἐνετείλατο; Psa.91.11, יְצַוֶּה → ἐντελεῖται; ἐντέλλομαι renders the verb ×325

evidence.note: Psa 91:11 quoted: “he will command (ἐντελεῖται) his angels concerning you”. Also Luk 4:10.
“God commanded (ἐνετείλατο), saying, Honour your father and your mother”: Exo 20:12, of which Deu 5:16 says “as Yahweh your God commanded you”.
“As the Father commanded me (ἐνετείλατο), so I do.”
“Teaching them to keep all that I commanded you”: the words of Deu 4:2 and 13:1 in Jesus' mouth.
“You are my friends, if you do what I command you.”

evidence.locator: Exo.39.1, כַּאֲשֶׁר צִוָּה יַהְוֶה → καθάπερ συνέταξεν κύριος; συντάσσω renders the verb ×85

evidence.note: “As the Lord directed me (καθὰ συνέταξέν μοι κύριος)”: the refrain “as Yahweh commanded” in its Greek dress.
“The disciples did as Jesus directed them.”

parallels.note: “Say”: Yahweh's commanding is his speaking; what he says, is.
“Speak”: “I did not speak to your fathers, nor command them”; “which I did not command, nor speak”.
“Send”: the true prophet is sent and commanded; of the false, “I did not send them, nor command them, nor speak to them”.
“Do”: the answer to a command. “According to all that God commanded him, so he did.”

phrases.gloss: which I am commanding you today (Moses in Deuteronomy)
give charge to one's house (before dying)
which I did not command (of worship men devised)

words.summary: The thing commanded, about 180 times, often as the verb's own object (“the commandment which Yahweh commanded you”, 1Sa 13:13). Beside its neighbours it names Yahweh's requirement by where it comes from, the word of one who has the right to be obeyed: חֹק is what is cut in and fixed, מִשְׁפָּט what is ruled by a judge, עֵדוּת what is witnessed, תּוֹרָה what is taught; מִצְוָה is what is ordered.

senses.gloss: command, order (of a king, a father, a leader)
senses.definition: What a man in authority has ordered: a king's order to his people, a father's charge to his sons, the arrangements David left for the Levites and singers. Also the terms of a deed, and what is due to someone by order.

evidence.note: “They were silent and answered him not a word, for it was מִצְוַת הַמֶּלֶךְ, saying, You shall not answer him”: the command is quoted. So 2Ki 18:36.
The sons of Jonadab “have listened to the מִצְוָה of their father”, namely what he “commanded his sons, not to drink wine”. So Jer 35:16, 18.
“Why do you transgress the king's command?”
Solomon to Shimei: “the command that I commanded you”.
“Keep, my son, the commandment of your father, and do not forsake the law of your mother.”
The Levites praised “by the commandment of David the man of God”. So Neh 12:45; 2Ch 8:14; 29:25; 35:10.
“The king's command was upon them”, a fixed provision for the singers.
The tithes are “מִצְוַת הַלְוִיִּם”: what is the Levites' by command.
The sealed deed of purchase, “the מִצְוָה and the statutes”: its binding terms.
“Their fear of me is מִצְוַת אֲנָשִׁים, learned”: a command of men set where Yahweh's should be. Quoted in Mat 15:9 and Mrk 7:7.

senses.definition: What Yahweh has commanded, to be kept and done: one particular order, the whole charge given through Moses, or (in the plural) all his commandments.

evidence.note: “These are הַמִּצְוֹת which Yahweh commanded Moses for the sons of Israel in Mount Sinai”: the noun defined by its verb. So Num 36:13.

senses.definition: One order of Yahweh to one man or about one matter.

evidence.note: To Saul: “you have not kept the מִצְוָה of Yahweh your God which he commanded you”, to wait for Samuel.
To the man of God: “you have not kept the commandment which Yahweh your God commanded you”, not to eat bread in Bethel.
A soul that sins by error “in any of the commandments of Yahweh which are not to be done”: prohibitions, one by one. So Lev 4:13.
“He has despised the word of Yahweh and broken his commandment.”
“And now, O priests, this commandment is for you.”

senses.definition: The singular with the article for all that Yahweh charged Israel with through Moses, taken as one.

evidence.note: “This is הַמִּצְוָה, the statutes and the judgments, which Yahweh your God commanded to teach you”: one commandment, whose content is the statutes and judgments. So Deu 5:31; 7:11.
“This commandment which I command you today is not too hard for you, nor is it far off … the word is very near you, in your mouth and in your heart, to do it” (verse 14).
“All the commandment which I command you today you shall keep to do, that you may live.”
The king is not to “turn aside from the commandment, right or left”.
“The tablets of stone, and the law and the commandment, which I have written.”
“The commandment of Yahweh is pure, enlightening the eyes.”
“I have seen an end of all perfection; your commandment is exceedingly broad.”
“The commandment is a lamp, and the law is light.”
Asa told Judah “to do the law and the commandment”.
“The law is holy, and the commandment (ἡ ἐντολή) holy and just and good.”

senses.definition: All that Yahweh has commanded, as the many things to be kept: said with “keep”, “do”, “listen to”, “remember”, and of those who love him.

evidence.note: “Showing mercy to thousands, to those who love me and keep מִצְוֹתָי.” So Deu 5:10; 7:9; Neh 1:5; Dan 9:4.
“Fear God and keep his commandments, for this is the whole of man.”
Abraham “listened to my voice and kept my charge, my commandments, my statutes and my laws”.
“If you walk in my statutes and keep my commandments and do them”; verses 14 and 15 the reverse, which breaks the covenant.
The tassel is to be looked on, “and you shall remember all the commandments of Yahweh and do them”.
The blessing, “if you listen to the commandments of Yahweh your God”; the curse if not (verse 28).
“I delight in your commandments, which I love.” So Psa 119:127; 112:1.
“All your commandments are faithfulness”; verse 151, “truth”; verse 172, “righteousness”.
“O that you had attended to my commandments! Then your peace would have been as a river.”
“If you would enter into life, keep the commandments (τὰς ἐντολάς)”, and Jesus then names them from Exo 20.

evidence.locator: Deu.6.1, הַמִּצְוָה → αἱ ἐντολαί; Deu.30.11, הַמִּצְוָה → ἡ ἐντολή; ἐντολή renders מִצְוָה ×97

evidence.note: “Which is the great commandment in the law?” Jesus answers from Deu 6:5, the chapter that opens “this is the commandment” (Deu 6:1). The Peshitta has ܦܘܩܕܢܐ, of another root. Also Mrk 12:29, 30.
“Why do you transgress the commandment of God because of your tradition?”, the commandment being Exo 20:12. Also Mrk 7:8, 9.
“Honour your father and mother, which is the first commandment with promise”: Exo 20:12; Deu 5:16.
The commandments of Exo 20, “and if there is any other commandment”, summed up in “you shall love your neighbour as yourself”.
“If you love me, keep my commandments”: love and keeping joined as in Exo 20:6.
“This is the love of God, that we keep his commandments; and his commandments are not burdensome”: compare Deu 30:11.
“His commandment is life everlasting.”
The saints “keep the commandments of God and the faith of Jesus”. So Rev 12:17.
Isa 29:13 quoted: “in vain they worship me, teaching as doctrines commandments of men (ἐντάλματα ἀνθρώπων)”. Also Mrk 7:7.
“According to the commandments and teachings of men”: Isaiah's phrase again.

parallels.note: “Statute”, what is cut in and fixed (also חֻקָּה): the commonest companion. “The commandment, the statutes and the judgments” is Deuteronomy's name for the whole.
“Judgment”, what a judge rules: the third of Deuteronomy's three.
“Law, instruction”: the pair “the law and the commandment”, and in Proverbs a parent's teaching beside his command.
“Testimony” (plural עֵדֹת): what Yahweh has borne witness to, beside what he has ordered.

evidence.note: “The commandments of Yahweh your God, and his testimonies and his statutes.”
All four together: “his statutes, his commandments, his judgments and his testimonies, as written in the law of Moses”.
Law, testimony, precepts, commandment, fear and judgments of Yahweh, six in a row.

parallels.note: “Word”: the commandment is Yahweh's word, the word of his lips.

evidence.note: “The commandment of his lips” beside “the words of his mouth”.

opposites.note: Forsaking the commandments of Yahweh is set against going after the Baals and other gods.

words.summary: Nine times in two places only: eight in the saying of Isa 28:10, repeated in verse 13, and once in Hos 5:11. Half the tokens counted under it are the verb's imperative צַו (“command!”, Lev 6:2), spelled alike. Its meaning rests on Isa 28:13, where it is a piece of “the word of Yahweh”; Hos 5:11 is too short to fix a sense by itself.

senses.definition: One order at a time: in Isaiah the word of Yahweh given “precept on precept, line on line, here a little, there a little”, as teaching is given to a child just weaned (Isa 28:9); in Hosea a command that Ephraim chose to walk after, by the context a command of men.

evidence.note: “The word of Yahweh shall be to them צַו לָצָו צַו לָצָו, line on line, line on line, here a little, there a little”: צַו is what the word of Yahweh comes as, piece by piece.
The same words, after “whom will he teach knowledge? … those weaned from milk” (verse 9): teaching in the smallest steps. Verse 11, of the other tongue, is quoted in 1Co 14:21.
“Ephraim is oppressed, crushed in judgment, because he was willing, he walked after צָו.” Compare Mic 6:16, “the statutes of Omri are kept”.

parallels.note: “Line”, the measuring line: precept on precept is matched by line on line.

words.summary: Three times: a thing set up to be seen, by a road to show the way or over the dead to show where they lie. Arabic ṣuwwa is the same thing, stones set up as a sign for travellers, and its plural is used of graves. How it belongs with “command” is not clear: perhaps as what directs the traveller, but no verse shows that, and it rests on three uses and one sure cognate.

senses.gloss: marker set up by a road or a grave
senses.definition: Something set up or built so as to be seen and to point: waymarks along a highway for those who will come back by it, a marker built beside a dead man's bone until it is buried, the monument over a prophet's grave.

evidence.note: “Set up for yourself צִיֻּנִים, make for yourself guideposts (תַּמְרוּרִים); set your heart to the highway, the way you went”: set up, beside a road, to mark the way back.
“When one sees a man's bone, he shall build a צִיּוּן beside it, until the buriers have buried it”: built, visible, marking where the dead lie.
Josiah: “What is this צִיּוּן that I see?” “It is the grave of the man of God who came from Judah.”

evidence.locator: Ezk.39.15, צִיּוּן → σημεῖον (once; 2Ki.23.17 has σκόπελον and Jer.31.21 reads the word as Σιων)

evidence.note: The common New Testament word for a sign; no passage with צִיּוּן is quoted there.

cognates.gloss: enjoin, charge, bid, order, command (also أَوْصَى awṣā)
cognates.note: The same three consonants as the Hebrew, ṣ, w and a weak third, with the first two in the other order (w-ṣ-y for ṣ-w-y), and the same sense in the same doubled stem: to lay a charge on someone. The reciprocal tawāṣaw is “they charged one another”. The ṣ is plain ṣ.

evidence.note: “He enjoined him; charged him; bade him; ordered him: he commanded him, بِكَذَا, to do such a thing.”

cognates.note: The noun of waṣṣā, as מִצְוָה is of צִוָּה: a charge or command, and in particular a man's last charge, his will; awṣā is “he made his will”, and the waṣī is the one commissioned to carry it out. Compare the dying man's charge to his house (Gen 49:29; 2Ki 20:1).

evidence.locator: p. 3055 (Supplement), art. وصى: وَصِيَّةٌ (n44627), أَوْصَى (n44624), وَصِىٌّ (n44626)
evidence.note: “An injunction, a charge, bidding, order, or command … And A will, or testament”; “أَوْصَى He made his will”; “A person commissioned … an executor appointed by a will.”

cognates.gloss: sign of stones set up to guide travellers; (plural) graves
cognates.note: The thing צִיּוּן names, in both its uses: stones set up in the way through an unknown desert (Jer 31:21), and in the plural, graves (2Ki 23:17; Ezk 39:15). The verb ṣawwā is “he made waymarks in the way”. The root is ṣ-w-w, with the same plain ṣ as waṣṣā.

evidence.note: “A sign for the guidance of travellers, consisting of stones, set up in the way in an unknown desert … Hence [the pl.] أَصْوَآءٌ is applied to signify Graves”; “He made صُوًى [i. e. signs set up for the guidance of travellers] in the way.”

cognates.note: The Targum's word at Ezk 39:15. It may be the Hebrew word carried over and not an Aramaic word of its own, so it is marked possible. Later Hebrew has the verb צִיֵּן from the noun, “to mark” graves.

evidence.note: “Targ. Ez. XXXIX, 15”; the Hebrew: “heap of stones, mark, esp. the mark put up to indicate the neighborhood of an unclean place.”

doctrine.statement: The first command in scripture is to the man: “Yahweh God commanded the man, saying, Of every tree of the garden you may freely eat, but of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil you shall not eat, for in the day that you eat of it you shall surely die” (Gen 2:16–17). When he had eaten, Yahweh asked, “have you eaten of the tree which I commanded you not to eat of?” (Gen 3:11), and passed sentence “because you … ate of the tree which I commanded you, saying, You shall not eat of it”: toil, “until you return to the ground, for out of it you were taken; for dust you are, and to dust you shall return” (Gen 3:17, 19). Paul reads it so: “through one man sin entered into the world, and death through sin”, “through the disobedience of the one man the many were made sinners” (Rom 5:12, 19). From the verses: death is the sentence for breaking God's command, and it is a return to dust; nothing in the sentence speaks of a part of man that lives on.

“By the word of Yahweh the heavens were made, and by the breath of his mouth all their host … he spoke, and it was; he commanded, and it stood” (Psa 33:6, 9). Sun, moon, stars and the waters above the heavens are to praise him, “for he commanded, and they were created” (Psa 148:5); “I made the earth and created man upon it; my hands stretched out the heavens, and all their host I commanded” (Isa 45:12). The commandment of the sabbath gives the time: “in six days Yahweh made the heavens and the earth, the sea, and all that is in them, and rested the seventh day” (Exo 20:11). Hebrews says the same: “the ages were framed by the word of God” (Heb 11:3). From the verses: the heavens and the earth came to be at God's command, each thing standing when he spoke, in six days.

Yahweh said to Moses, “I will raise up for them a prophet from among their brothers, like you, and I will put my words in his mouth, and he shall speak to them all that I command him” (Deu 18:18). Peter and Stephen say this prophet is Jesus (Act 3:22–23; 7:37). Jesus says of himself, “I have not spoken from myself, but the Father who sent me gave me a commandment, what I should say and what I should speak” (Jhn 12:49); “this commandment I received from my Father” (Jhn 10:18); “as the Father commanded me, so I do” (Jhn 14:31); “I have kept my Father's commandments and remain in his love” (Jhn 15:10). From the verses: Jesus is a man raised up from among his brothers, who stands under God's command as Moses did, receives it, keeps it, and speaks only what he is given. The one who commands is the Father; the son is the one commanded.

Yahweh shows mercy “to those who love me and keep my commandments” (Exo 20:6), and Moses joins the two: “you shall love Yahweh your God and keep his charge, his statutes, his judgments and his commandments always” (Deu 11:1). The commandment “is not too hard for you, nor is it far off … the word is very near you, in your mouth and in your heart, to do it” (Deu 30:11, 14), which Paul calls “the word of faith which we preach” (Rom 10:8). The end of the matter is “fear God and keep his commandments, for this is the whole of man” (Ecc 12:13). Jesus says the same of himself and of his disciples: “if you love me, keep my commandments” (Jhn 14:15), and John, “this is the love of God, that we keep his commandments, and his commandments are not burdensome” (1Jn 5:3); the saints are those who “keep the commandments of God and the faith of Jesus” (Rev 14:12). From the verses: love of God is shown by keeping what he has commanded, under Moses and under Christ alike, and what he commands can be done.

Moses charged Israel, “you shall not add to the word which I command you, nor take from it” (Deu 4:2; 13:1). Yahweh says of the worship men devised, “which I did not command, nor did it come into my heart” (Jer 7:31), and Nadab and Abihu died for offering fire “which he had not commanded them” (Lev 10:1). Of Judah he says, “their fear of me is a commandment of men, learned” (Isa 29:13). Jesus quotes this against the Pharisees: “why do you transgress the commandment of God because of your tradition? … In vain they worship me, teaching as doctrines commandments of men” (Mat 15:3, 9); “leaving the commandment of God, you hold the tradition of men” (Mrk 7:8). From the verses: what God has commanded is the measure of worship and teaching; what men add to it has no authority, and where it displaces his commandment the worship is vain.

note: Drafted 2026-11-15. Root key צוה as the brief keys it; no other entry has it. BDB's zero-token cross-references m.dc.ag, r.av.ah and r.bt.af are left out. The verb's lemma is given as the piel צִוָּה, since it has no qal. Shared tokens: the eight צַו of Isa 28:10, 13 without the preposition are counted under both r.az.aa and r.az.ad (four each way in the brief), and nine imperatives צַו of the verb (Lev 6:2; 24:2; Num 5:2; 28:2; 34:2; 35:2; Deu 2:4; 2Ki 20:1; Isa 38:1) are counted under r.az.ad by spelling; the noun's own uses are nine (Isa 28:10, 13 eight times, Hos 5:11). Jdg 13:14 צִוִּיתִיהָ has no stem in the corpus; it is piel. No personal name is formed from the root in names.jsonl. צִיּוֹן (Zion) is left out: its derivation is not known, and it is a place. Cognates: Arabic waṣṣā is recorded as cognate although its first two consonants stand in the other order; the reviewer should decide whether that should be `possible` (the support balance of the verb, מִצְוָה and צַו rests on it). Leads not followed, no locator verified: Syriac ṣwāyā “heap of stones” (Payne Smith); Jewish Aramaic צַוָּאָה “will, testament” (not found as a headword in the vendored Jastrow); the Aramaic metathesis parallel חוה / Arabic waḥā; Sabaic wṣy (Biella, not found in the OCR); Ugaritic and Phoenician not properly searched: only a headword grep of Krahmalkov’s OCR, which found nothing; Segert and Fisher still to check. The Greek forms quoted from Mat 15:4, Mat 27:10, Jhn 14:31 and the Septuagint of Exo 39:1 were written from memory and need checking against the texts. The Peshitta has no word of this root (it uses pqd, ܦܘܩܕܢܐ). Open questions: (1) Hos 5:11 צָו: read here as a command of men, by context only; the Septuagint read another word (“vanities”); (2) whether Isa 28:10 is the scoffers' mockery or the prophet's own words does not change the sense given, which rests on verse 13; (3) the tie of צִיּוּן to “command” is unexplained; (4) the σημεῖον rendering cites Mat 24:30 only as an instance of the Greek word; (5) doctrine items son-of-god and commandments-of-men are reasoned conclusions to review.
